title: Bir bakar mısın?
goal: Soften a request with bir, -sAnA, zahmet olmazsa and rica etsem, and choose the right register for the person in front of you.

intro.text: A night in front of the TV, and everyone wants something: the remote, the volume down, the subtitles on. *Bir bakar mısın?*, *Versene!* and *Zahmet olmazsa…* ask for the same kind of thing, but not of the same person.

vocab.en: trouble, bother (zahmet olmazsa: if it's no trouble)
fault (Kusura bakma: sorry, excuse me; polite: Kusura bakmayın)
favour; kindness (iyilik yapmak: to do a favour)
Excuse me. (to get attention or say sorry)

exercises.question: In a restaurant, you want the waiter's attention. What do you say?

why.1: `-sAnA` is for friends; to a waiter it's pushy.
why.2: A bare imperative sounds like an order.

exercises.explain: *Bir bakar mısınız?* is the standard way to call a waiter or a shop assistant.

exercises.en: Give me the remote, will you!

accept: sene

reject.why: *Ver-* has a front vowel, so the suffix is *-sene*: *versene*.

exercises.label: *oturmak* + `-sAnA`: sit down, why don't you (to one friend, to several)

accept: otursana
otursanıza
If it is no trouble, could you pass the salt?
If it is no trouble, could you pass me the salt?
If it is no trouble, would you pass the salt?
If it is no trouble, would you pass me the salt?
If it is no trouble, can you pass the salt?
If it is no trouble, can you pass me the salt?
If it is not too much trouble, could you pass the salt?
If it is not too much trouble, could you pass me the salt?
If it is not too much trouble, would you pass the salt?
If it is not too much trouble, would you pass me the salt?
If it is not too much trouble, can you pass the salt?
If it is not too much trouble, can you pass me the salt?
[Could|Would|Can] you pass (me) the salt if it is [no|not too much] trouble?
Would you mind passing (me) the salt?
exercises.explain: *Zahmet olmazsa* (if it isn't any trouble) before an aorist question: very polite.

exercises.prompt: Could you do me a favour?
accept: Bana bir iyilik yapar mısın?
Bana bir iyilik yapar mısınız?
(Bana) bir iyilik yapabilir misin(iz)?
Bir iyilik yapar mısın(ız)?
[Senden|Sizden] bir iyilik rica etsem?
exercises.explain: *İyilik yapmak* (to do a favour) in an aorist question, with *sen* or *siz*.

exercises.question: Which request is the most formal?

why.1: Polite and neutral, but less formal than *rica ederim* after a `-mA` clause.

exercises.explain: *-mAnızı rica ederim* belongs to letters, notices and announcements.

exercises.prompt: Excuse me, could you speak a little more slowly?
exercises.text: Affedersiniz, biraz daha yavaş konuşabilir misiniz?

exercises.en: Could I have a glass of water, please?

accept: sem

reject.why: *Rica etsen* is **if you asked**. You are asking for yourself: *rica etsem*.

exercises.explain: *Rica etsem?* (literally **if I requested**) is a polite, slightly formal request.

accept: Stop shouting, the baby is sleeping!
Stop shouting, the baby is asleep!
Do not shout, the baby is [sleeping|asleep]!
Quit shouting, the baby is [sleeping|asleep]!
Will you stop shouting, the baby is [sleeping|asleep]!
Stop shouting, will you, the baby is [sleeping|asleep]!
exercises.explain: `-mAsAnA`, the negative of `-sAnA`, asks someone to stop: *bağırmasana*.

exercises.prompt: Sit down, why don't you! (to a friend)
accept: Otursana!
Otursana ya!
Hadi otursana!

reject.why: *Oturun* is a plain, polite imperative. **Why don't you** to a friend is the friendly push `-sAnA`: *otursana*.

exercises.en: If it's no trouble, could you close the door?

exercises.prompt: Is the film dubbed or subtitled?
accept: Film dublajlı mı, altyazılı mı?
Film dublajlı mı yoksa altyazılı mı?

exercises.task: Your neighbour, an older man you don't know well, watches TV very loudly late at night. Write him a polite note (two or three sentences) asking him to turn it down. Use at least two softeners.
models: Amca, kusura bakmayın, rahatsız ediyorum. Gece televizyonun sesi bizim daireden çok duyuluyor. Zahmet olmazsa saat on birden sonra sesi biraz kısabilir misiniz? Çok teşekkürler.

Merhaba, ben üst kattaki komşunuz Elif. Affedersiniz, akşamları televizyonun sesi çok yüksek oluyor ve bebeğimiz uyuyamıyor. Mümkünse geceleri sesi biraz kısar mısınız? Anlayışınız için teşekkür ederim.
checklist: An apology before the request: *Kusura bakmayın*, *Affedersiniz*
At least two softeners: *zahmet olmazsa*, *mümkünse*, *bir*, `-(y)AbilIr misiniz?`, *biraz*
Thanks at the end: *Çok teşekkürler*, *Teşekkür ederim*
